items.q: Earl King, I just helped him out with it. ... I had to rearrange some of the things. To fit what I was putting into his song you know.

items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: The transcript mentions Professor Longhair only as an artist who recorded Earl King's songs ('his songs have been recorded by artists such as ... Professor Longhair'). There is no direct interaction, collaboration, or personal relationship described between Earl King and Professor Longhair in the te

ctx.x: To sum it up, I think I can say that he is the most active researcher and writer on New Orleans rhythm and blues, so he can really work well tonight with our musician prayer. This is Ted Jones. This is a book that is written by an Englishman. This little booklet, this magazine, also comes from a footnote dedicated to New Orleans music, mainly the drafts. Now this isn't the only little booklet that has a magazine that has anything to do with rhythm and blues, but I find it interesting that the jazz one is…
Like you said, the Irish Channel, mid-part, Washington, and the council of that vicinity. I've spent that quite a bit of my life.
